title: Type I and Type II as named testing mistakes
dek: Wikipedia: false rejection versus false retention. Size α and power 1−β. Design lives on stats-power.
story: Type I/II on Wikipedia are named mistakes in a Neyman–Pearson world: reject a true H0 (I, size α) versus fail to reject a false H0 (II, β). Power is 1−β at a specified alternative.
stats-power already designs n. This card is the encyclopedia pair so 'we were underpowered' is attached to a named β, not a vibe.
FDR is not Type I. A q-value is not α. Do not mix the dictionaries.
deep: α is a property of a procedure under H0, not of a single p-value after the fact (though people treat p<α as a Type I ritual).
Power needs a specific H1: a 1.1-fold risk is not a 3-fold risk.
Multiple testing changes the Type I object (family vs per-test).
Diagnostic false-positive/negative rhyme but are not hypothesis tests unless you force them to be.

steps.title: Name β at a specified OR
p=0.06 is not proof of H0
Type II is the miss risk, not a posterior

example.takeaway: Type II is a miss at a named alternative. It is not P(H0).

choices: Failing to reject a false H0
Type II β=0.2 at that named alternative, not at every alternative
